steps.name: DESeq2 interaction-model differential expression
steps.context: counts.csv is 12000 genes x 25 columns (24 samples + gene id) from salmon; metadata.csv has condition, time, time_hours. 2 conditions x 4 time points (t0..t3) x 3 replicates.
steps.question: Which genes show a treatment-specific change over t0-t3 beyond the shared time trend (condition:time interaction) in the 2x4 cell-line RNA-seq design?
steps.description: Load counts.csv (12,000 genes x 24 samples) and metadata.csv (condition, time, time_hours) into a DESeq2/PyDESeq2 design. Fit the additive model ~condition + time and the full model ~condition + time + condition:time (condition and time as factors; t0 reference). The interaction term isolates treatment-specific deviations from the shared time trend. Use likelihood-ratio test (full vs reduced) for the omnibus time-dependent treatment effect, plus Wald tests on per-time-point interaction contrasts (t1,t2,t3 vs t0) for directionality.
acceptance_criteria: DESeqDataSet built from counts.csv with design ~ condition + time + condition:time, releveling t0 as reference
prefiltering removes genes with tiny counts; diagnostic size-factor dispersion summaries reported
results() for the interaction term (or LRT comparing to ~condition+time) produced and saved as CSV with log2FC, p-value, padj

steps.name: Shrink interaction LFCs and summarize top genes
steps.context: PyDESeq2 supports LFC shrinkage; alternatively report raw MLE LFCs and note the shrinkage status. 12k genes is small enough for per-contrast shrinkage.
steps.question: What are the effect sizes and temporal patterns of the treatment-specific interaction genes?
steps.description: Apply log2FC shrinkage where available on the interaction contrasts, assemble a ranked gene table (gene id, per-time-point interaction log2FCs, Wald/LRT stats, FDR), and produce MA and volcano plots plus a heatmap of top interaction genes across the 24 samples.
acceptance_criteria: Shrunken LFCs computed for interaction contrasts and exported
Combined table (gene, base stats, per-time-point interaction effects, padj) written
MA/volcano-style plots of the interaction LRT/Wald results saved
Number of genes passing FDR < 0.05 reported

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of interaction genes
steps.context: Reference available at /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt (HGNC symbols). Counts carry gene symbols or ids from salmon — map to HGNC symbols first; UniProt human idmapping at /mnt/refs/managed/uniprot-idmapping-human/current/ can bridge identifiers if needed. If symbol mapping coverage is poor, report the gap rather than forcing enrichment.
steps.question: Which biological pathways show treatment-specific temporal perturbation among the interaction genes?
steps.description: Take the significant condition:time interaction genes and test over-representation against the WikiPathways human GMT (HGNC symbols) using the tested genes as background (gseapy ORA). Report pathways whose perturbation response is treatment-specific.
acceptance_criteria: GMT parsed from WikiPathways Homo sapiens with readable set names
Over-representation of FDR-significant interaction genes (and, separately, direction-stratified up/down lists) computed with background = tested genes
Results table with pathway name, overlap, adjusted p-value saved; report is annotated with any gene-symbol-to-GMT mapping coverage caveat

plan.title: Treatment-by-time interaction DE in cell-line RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is 2 conditions x 4 time points (t0..t3), 3 replicates each, 12,000-gene salmon counts. The research question is specifically about genes whose time course differs between conditions, so the core analysis fits a DESeq2-style GLM with an explicit condition:time interaction; the LRT against the additive model (~condition + time) tests the omnibus treatment-specific temporal effect, and per-time-point Wald contrasts give directionality. Shrunken LFCs, plots, and a ranked table summarize the hits, and a WikiPathways human over-representation analysis (HGNC symbols, tested genes as background) annotates which pathways are treatment-specifically perturbed.
